title: Build Your Own Team of Managed Agents - Jack Wotherspoon, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: Jack Wotherspoon presents Gemini's managed/cloud agents: a single API call spins up a cloud sandbox with a harness, file system, tools, credentials proxy, and triggers. The main transferable ideas are decoupling conversation state (interactions) from file-system state (environments) to enable multi-agent handoffs with fresh context, and keeping secrets out of the sandbox via a proxy that injects tokens.

takeaways.what_they_do: They split state into 'interactions' (conversation) and 'environments' (sandbox file system), so a second agent can reuse the same files with a fresh context window.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it has a very fresh kind of context window and conversation, but it's reusing the environment

takeaways.what_they_do: A proxy sits between sandbox and API, placing dummy placeholder tokens in the sandbox and injecting real credentials only when matching outbound API calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: secrets never actually enter the sandbox ... it puts a placeholder kind of dummy token into the sandbox

takeaways.technique: Reproducible cloud sandbox with mounted skills/agents.md
takeaways.what_they_do: They upload agents.md, skills, and a GitHub repo into a cloud sandbox at startup so runs are reproducible and don't touch the host machine.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can upload your different agents.md files, your skills, and kind of run through the playbooks

takeaways.what_they_do: Triggers wake an agent on a schedule (e.g., 8:30am) to run a task and post results via webhook/Slack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you could set a trigger. The managed agent would essentially wake up, run its task

takeaways.technique: Narrow single-purpose agents fanned out via API
takeaways.what_they_do: One agent calls other managed agents as API calls, each with one narrow purpose writing to files, so tasks are measurable and controllable.
A one-line config sets the model per managed agent: fast model for quick tasks, reasoning model for analysis.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you're wanting to do something that needs to be fast and efficient, you can use Gemini Flash
